setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the example MIDI device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4. The scale is C major, a MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Map scale to white keys is off, its default. The sequencer is stopped, so the keyboard plays the channel's output directly. The norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Play the white keys C, D, E, F, G, A, B, then the black keys between them. With Map scale to white keys off every key sends its own pitch: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71 for the white keys, with 61, 63, 66, 68, 70 for the black keys. The strip below lists the notes in the order you played them.
steps.title: Raw notes by default

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC, open the MIDI controller options and turn Map scale to white keys On. The row now reads On.
steps.title: Turn the mapping on

steps.caption: Leave PARAMS and play the white keys again. They now follow the selected scale with its root on C: in C major C D E F G A B C sound as 60 62 64 65 67 69 71 72, the same pitches as before. What changes is the black keys: each one repeats the white key above it, so C# sounds 62 instead of 61.
steps.title: White keys follow the scale

steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8), turn E3 two detents to change the scale from Major to natural minor and press K3, then tap Channel (3,8). Play the white keys: C D Eb F G Ab Bb C sound as 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72. Black keys still repeat the white key above them: C# plays 62 and D# plays 63. Read the strip below for the thirteen keys C to C: 60 62 62 63 63 65 67 67 68 68 70 70 72, the eight white keys being 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72.
steps.title: Change the scale, change the keys

steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Turn E2 once and E3 to set the scale degree to II, press K3, turn E2 three detents and E3 to set rotation 2, press K3, then raise the transposition fader (the minimum at (9,8), then (16,8) fourteen times) to +2. Press Channel (3,8) and play the white keys C to C. All three Honour options are still Off, so the keys follow plain natural minor: look in the strip for 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72, with each black key repeating the white key above it.
steps.title: Set degree II, rotation 2 and +2

steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC > MIDI controller options and turn Honour scale degree On, leave PARAMS and play the keys again. The seven white keys now start on degree II, so the whole run shifts: read the new notes in the strip below.
steps.title: Honour scale degree

steps.caption: Turn Honour scale rotations On as well and play the keys again. Rotation 2 drops the last two of the seven positions by an octave: compare the strip with the previous step.
steps.title: Add rotation

steps.caption: Turn Honour scale transpose On too and play the keys again. Everything now sounds two semitones higher than in the previous step.
steps.title: Add transposition

steps.caption: Turn Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations Off and play, then Honour scale transpose Off, and finally turn Map scale to white keys Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC. Press Channel (3,8) and play C to C: every key plays its own pitch once more, 60 to 72, whatever scale is selected.
steps.title: Turn mapping off

title: Let a keyboard follow the scale
